gloss: to value; to respect; to attach importance to

definitions.gloss: to value; to respect; to attach importance to
definitions.explanation: To regard something as important or worthy of respect. Used for abstract concepts like traditions, principles, and values rather than physical objects.

examples.japanese: {伝統|でんとう}を{重|おも}んじる。
この{会社|かいしゃ}は{社員|しゃいん}の{意見|いけん}を{重|おも}んじている。
examples.english: This company values the opinions of its employees.

examples.japanese: {個人|こじん}の{自由|じゆう}を{重|おも}んじる{社会|しゃかい}を{目指|めざ}すべきだ。
examples.english: We should aim for a society that respects individual freedom.

notes:
An ichidan verb derived from {重|おも}い (heavy, important). An older variant {重|おも}んずる also exists and conjugates as a mixed verb (ずる-verb), but {重|おも}んじる is the standard modern form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {伝統|でんとう}を{重|おも}んじる (to value tradition)
- {礼儀|れいぎ}を{重|おも}んじる (to value manners)
- {人権|じんけん}を{重|おも}んじる (to respect human rights)
- {意見|いけん}を{重|おも}んじる (to value opinions)
- {名誉|めいよ}を{重|おも}んじる (to value honor)

A formal, written-style verb. More elevated than {大切|たいせつ}にする (to treat as important) or {尊重|そんちょう}する (to respect). Typically used with abstract nouns like traditions, values, rights, and principles.
